**memra today** (`crates/memra-server/src/worker.rs:134-176`, `crates/memra-kv/src/lib.rs`): KV prefix reuse = a GPU-resident parked-session LRU pool (`MEMRA_REUSE_POOL`, default **2** whole caches per model), append-only exact-extension matching only. Quantized KV (q8_0/q5_1/FP8-e4m3) in-place. Snapshot/rollback exists. No host/disk tier, no sub-prefix matching, no compressed-at-rest format.

**Mechanisms LMCache has that memra is missing** (single-GPU, one-model relevant only; PD disaggregation, P2P/multi-node, multi-engine sharing excluded as N/A):

1. **CPU-RAM KV offload tier (pinned host) behind the parked pool** — highest value. memra's reuse hits die when the 2-deep VRAM pool evicts; LMCache's core win is that evicted prefixes park in host RAM and reload over PCIe far faster than recompute (this is most of their TTFT/throughput claim for multi-turn/agentic). Portability: excellent — memra already owns bounded pinned host buffers, positioned reads, and CUDA-owner-thread H2D discipline from the expert-spill lane; bytes are exact so argmax/spec gates are unaffected. Also frees VRAM currently pinned by parked caches. Do layer-wise pipelined reload (H2D layer i+1 while prefilling layer i) to hide transfer.

2. **Chunk-hashed, token-granular cache keys** — LMCache hashes fixed-size token chunks (~256) so *any* request sharing a prefix gets a partial hit at chunk granularity, across sessions and callers. memra only extends a whole parked session exactly. Exact-bytes, gate-safe; mostly a keying/index change plus partial-prefill of the unmatched suffix (which memra's prefill path already supports). Directly attacks the expert-prefill-bound losing cells for any workload with shared system prompts.

3. **Local-NVMe third tier with persistence** — KV survives process restart and long idle (agent sessions, big system prompts). Same storage-to-compute machinery as the spill lane (O_DIRECT/io_uring learnings apply verbatim); exact bytes. Value is workload-dependent — only pays when host RAM tier overflows or restarts matter.

4. **Async/overlapped KV store-out** — offload KV to host as layers complete during prefill/decode instead of only at session retire, so tier-writes never sit on the critical path. Small, complements #1.

5. **CacheGen-style compressed at-rest KV** (delta encoding across adjacent tokens + layer-sensitivity-aware arithmetic coding, GPU-side decode) — only matters once tier #3's bandwidth is the bottleneck; it's *lossy*, so it conflicts with memra's exactness gates. memra's FP8/q8 KV already gives 2-4x; mark as low-priority, opt-in-flag-only.

6. **CacheBlend non-prefix reuse** (reuse RAG-chunk KV at arbitrary positions, selectively recompute ~15% highest-KV-deviation tokens) — largest TTFT lever for RAG-shaped prompts, but approximate by construction: breaks the argmax gate. Research-arm only, never a default under memra's exactness-first doctrine.

7. **KV/hit-rate observability** (request- and token-level prefix-hit metrics) — cheap counters; needed anyway to prove #1-#3 on the board.

**Priority for the board**: #1 + #2 (exact-bytes, reuse existing spill infrastructure, directly reduce expert-prefill work on the two losing H100 cells for multi-turn workloads — though not the cold single-shot pp512 cell, which remains a GEMM problem), then #4, #3. #5/#6 are quality-traded and gated off by default.

MoE inference optimization literature survey (arxiv 2024-2026), grouped by the five requested areas.

## 1. Grouped/batched expert GEMM

- **MegaBlocks: Efficient Sparse Training with MoE** (2211.15841, 2022/23, foundational) — Reformulates expert computation as block-sparse GEMM ("dropless MoE"), no token padding/dropping, variable-size expert groups mapped to fixed 128-wide blocks. ~40% over Tutel, 2.4x over dense-padded frameworks. Portability: memra's CSR expert-major pair grouping is already the same idea in spirit; the block-sparse tile mapping (assign tiles to experts by CSR row extents rather than per-expert kernels) is the direct ancestor of the cublasGemmGroupedBatchedEx lane and the reference for handling load imbalance without padding waste.
- **SonicMoE: Accelerating MoE with IO- and Tile-aware Optimizations** (2512.14080, Dec 2025, Tri Dao group) — Fuses the token gather into GEMM activation loading, fuses SwiGLU into the epilogue, and "tile-aware token rounding" to minimize padding waste in grouped GEMM. 1.86x compute throughput vs ScatterMoE BF16 on H100; 25% forward speedup vs DeepGEMM on Blackwell; +1.16x kernel gain under high sparsity. Kernels open-sourced. **Highest-value paper for the prefill-bound board losses**: gather-fusion + epilogue-fusion port directly to the int8 MMQ kernel and the f16 grouped lane (memra currently dequants then GEMMs — a separate gather/dequant pass is exactly what SonicMoE shows is the IO tax). Blackwell numbers make it directly relevant to sm_120a.
- **TritonMoE: Cross-Platform Fused MoE Dispatch in Triton** (2605.23911, 2026) — Fully fused router+permute+grouped-GEMM+combine in Triton; fused gate+up GEMM from shared L2 tiles cuts global traffic 35%. 89-131% of MegaBlocks on A100 at ≤512-token batches; loses to block-sparse layout under extreme Zipf skew with 64+ experts (fixed BLOCK_M tiles). Portability: the gate+up fusion (one input-tile load feeds both projections) is a cheap, concrete win for memra's per-expert prefill GEMMs; the imbalance finding warns that fixed-tile grouped kernels degrade exactly on skewed CSR groups — measure per-group tile occupancy.

## 2. Expert offload / caching / prefetch

- **Pre-gated MoE** (2308.12066, ISCA 2024) — Trains a pre-gate so layer N computes layer N+1's routing, enabling perfect one-layer-ahead prefetch. ~1.5x+ throughput vs on-demand GPU offload, near GPU-resident latency. Portability: requires fine-tuning the router — off-limits for memra's frozen GGUF checkpoints, but the one-layer-lookahead *slot* in the schedule is the right overlap window for the SLRU spill path.
- **SiDA-MoE** (MLSys 2024) — Offline hash predicts expert activation from embeddings (data-aware). Up to 3.93x throughput, 75% memory saving, ~1% accuracy tradeoff. Portability: prediction accuracy is model-dependent; superseded conceptually by the routing-consistency paper below.
- **ExpertFlow (predictive caching)** (2410.17954, v2 2026, DAC'26) — T5-style single-pass predictor estimates expert usage across *all* layers at once (removes layer-by-layer predictor dependency), plus routing-path-aware token scheduling. Up to 93.7% GPU memory reduction, up to 10x over offloading baselines, single GPU. Portability: the all-layers-in-one-shot prediction idea beats per-layer lookahead for prefetch depth; heavy predictor though — memra's SLRU already wins on fits-VRAM models, this matters only for the Hy3 spill lane.
- **fMoE/FineMoE** (2502.05370, 2025) — Fine-grained per-expert offloading driven by expert-selection history + semantic hints from prompts. 47% latency reduction, 39% hit-rate improvement vs SOTA offloading. Portability: hit-rate-oriented eviction tuning ideas for the SLRU; system built on HF Transformers, so absolute numbers are soft.
- **HOBBIT** (2411.01433, 2024) — On a cache miss, load a *low-precision* version of non-critical experts instead of the full one; layer-level prefetch + multi-precision cache. Up to 9.93x decode speedup, implemented **in llama.cpp**. Portability: high — same runtime lineage as memra's GGUF world; "degrade-on-miss" is a natural extension of the Hy3 mixed Q2_K/NVFP4 tiering (cold experts can be spilled at lower bitwidth, cutting PCIe bytes on the exact path memra's spill lane measures).
- **PreScope/LayerScope** (2509.23638, ICS 2026) — Learnable layer-aware activation predictor + cross-layer prefetch scheduling + async I/O bubble elimination. +141% throughput, -74.6% latency vs SOTA offloading over PCIe. Portability: the *scheduling* formulation (globally balance prefetch cost vs on-demand load per layer) maps onto memra's storage-to-compute pipeline doctrine.
- **Not All Models Suit Expert Offloading (local routing consistency)** (2505.16056, 2025) — Measurement paper: defines SRP/SCH metrics over 20 MoE LLMs. Key findings: shared-expert architectures have *lower* local routing consistency; cache sweet spot ≈ **2x active experts per layer**; consistency is model-structural, not workload-dependent. Portability: directly actionable — compute SCH for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and Hy3 from existing router traces before sizing SLRU/spill caches; the 2x-top-k rule is a free starting point.
- **MoE-Infinity** (2401.14361) and **Fiddler** (2402.07033), 2024 — sequence-level activation-aware prefetch, and CPU-*compute* of cold experts instead of transferring weights (Mixtral on one 24GB GPU, ~8x vs offload baselines). Portability: Fiddler's insight (sometimes moving compute to the bytes beats moving bytes to compute) is worth one measured probe in the spill lane; contradicts memra's GPU-only assumption only when PCIe is the binding constraint.

## 3. Speculative decoding × MoE

- **Cohere: Why MoE Models Get More From Speculative Decoding** (blog, Apr 2026; best quantitative source found) — Measured expert overlap between adjacent verify tokens: **0.381 at distance 1** (3 of 8 experts shared, vs 0.118 independence baseline), decaying to ~0.30 at distance 4; mid-layers strongest (~0.50). Verifying 4 tokens loads only **~2.5x top-k unique experts, not 4x** (20.4 vs 25.4 predicted). Overlap is workload-invariant (0.377-0.386 across 13 Spec-Bench categories and 7 languages) — a structural property of routing. 1.95x BS=1 speedup; verify cost T(4)/T(1)=1.25x vs 1.46x Amdahl prediction. Portability: **direct evidence that MTP verify batches sublinearly inflate expert weight traffic** — memra's decode-side MTP already banks this; it also argues expert-prefill-style grouped kernels for the verify step pay off more than dense math predicts.
- **Cascade: Utility-Driven Speculative Decoding for MoE** (2506.20675, 2025) — The caution side: draft tokens collectively activate 2-3x more expert weights; naive speculation causes up to 1.5x *slowdowns*. Dynamic per-request K selection via a speculation-utility metric limits slowdown to 5%, +7-14% throughput over static K, in vLLM. Portability: memra's MTP K should be workload-adaptive, not fixed; cheap to implement (utility = accepted tokens / verify cost, already measurable).
- **SpecMoEOff** (2508.21706, 2025) — Uses speculative decoding *to hide offloading latency*: verify batches enlarge per-expert workload so compute covers expert transfer; roofline-guided GPU/CPU orchestration + CPU chunked-attention verify kernel. Up to 2.5x decode throughput over SOTA MoE offloading. Portability: **the exact mechanism the Hy3 spill lane wants** — spec-verify batching turns the spill path from bandwidth-bound toward compute-bound; combine with the Cohere overlap numbers to size the transfer budget.
- **EcoSpec: Less Experts, Faster Decoding** (2607.12696, Jul 2026) — Cost-aware draft-tree selection: prefer draft paths that reuse already-active experts (lightweight expert predictor + dynamic expert buffer), verification rule unchanged (exactness-safe). Up to 1.62x e2e on DeepSeek-V3.1/Qwen3-235B/GPT-OSS-120B. Portability: medium — draft-selection hook in memra's MTP could bias among near-equal candidates toward expert reuse; exactness gate compatible since target verification is untouched.
- **BlockFFN** (2507.08771, 2025) — Trains chunk-level activation sparsity so consecutive tokens share experts, explicitly for spec-decode friendliness. Portability: training-side, not applicable to frozen checkpoints; useful only as evidence that token-adjacent expert reuse is the lever.

## 4. Quantized MoE kernels / per-expert mixed precision

- **MxMoE** (2505.05799, 2025) — Co-designs per-linear-block precision assignment (using quantization sensitivity + expert activation frequency) with **auto-generated mixed-precision GroupGEMM kernels** that run different-precision GEMMs in parallel. 2.4 lower ppl than GPTQ at 2.25-bit; 3.4x over FP; 29.4% over uniform quant at matched accuracy (W5 A/W). Code: github.com/cat538/MxMoE. Portability: **closest published analog to memra's five-arm mixed Q2_K/Q3_K/NVFP4 study** — validates hot-expert-gets-more-bits ranking from activation frequency; their parallel mixed-precision grouped kernel is the counterexample to memra's current "mixed layers take the slow staged path" restriction.
- **DynaExq: Dynamic Expert Quantization** (2511.15015, 2025) — Online budget-constrained precision allocation: hot experts resident at high precision, cold experts low-precision fallback, async promote/demote with stable expert handles (never a partially-loaded expert on critical path). 73.09→77.57% accuracy vs static PTQ at equal HBM on Qwen3-80B; up to 2.73x vs offload baselines at BS=32. Portability: high conceptual overlap with SLRU + tier plans — the async promotion machinery and "budget-feasible top-n per layer" rule are a runtime version of memra's static v2 tier plans; a challenge to the frozen-plan assumption worth one arm of evidence.
- **MoPEQ** (2509.02512, 2025) — Post-training per-expert bitwidth assignment by expert sensitivity (VLM MoEs, Deepseek/Mixtral-class). Modest paper; useful mainly as accuracy-side corroboration that per-expert (not per-layer) precision is the right granularity.
- **TurboMind** (2508.15601, 2025) — Production INT4xFP16 GEMM kernel engineering + 8-bit KV; not MoE-specific but one of the few papers with real W4A16 kernel latency breakdowns to sanity-check MMQ's ~30TF effective against.

## 5. Single-GPU MoE serving throughput / roofline

- **MoE-Lightning** (2411.11217, ASPLOS 2025) — **Hierarchical Roofline Model (HRM)** spanning CPU-GPU-I/O + CGOPipe paged-weight pipelining; up to 10.3x over FlexGen-class on memory-constrained GPUs. Portability: HRM is the right formalism for memra's stated "measure the stages together" doctrine — it makes the spill pipeline's binding resource explicit per phase; worth reimplementing as an analysis notebook over existing JSONL data.
- **MoE-Lens** (2504.09345, 2025) — Throughput upper-bound model from CPU mem/GPU compute/workload interaction, 94% prediction accuracy, 4.6x avg (25.5x max) over SOTA. Portability: methodology paper — its "derive the hardware limit first, then measure gap-to-limit" is exactly the SOL-grinding style in memra's tuning campaign, extended to the offload regime.
- **MoE-Gen** (2503.09716, 2025) — Module-based batching: accumulate tokens in host memory, launch per-module (attention vs expert) optimal batch sizes. 8-31x over FlexGen/MoE-Lightning/DeepSpeed on single GPU, offline throughput regime. Portability: low for interactive serving (latency-hostile), but the observation that *expert modules want much larger batches than attention* supports memra's continuation batch-prime / concat-scheduler direction on the prefill side.

Cross-cutting takeaways for memra's two prefill-bound board losses: (a) SonicMoE-style gather+epilogue fusion into the grouped GEMM is the most portable published kernel win; (b) the Cohere overlap data (verify batch ≈ 2.5x top-k unique experts, structural and workload-invariant) plus SpecMoEOff argue MTP verify batching is a legitimate expert-traffic amortizer, with Cascade's dynamic-K as the guard; (c) MxMoE's parallel mixed-precision grouped kernels remove the justification for keeping mixed-layout layers off the fast path permanently; (d) run the 2505.16056 SCH metric on existing router traces before further SLRU/spill tuning — cache ≈ 2x active experts is the published sweet spot. Multi-node EP-only work (DeepEP, Speculative-MoE comm variants, ELDR PD-disaggregation) excluded per scope.

# MoE internals: llama.cpp + KTransformers — mechanism list with portability notes for memra

Sources read: `/tmp/llama.cpp` (master @ 2026-07-31) — `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/{mmq.cu,mmq.cuh,mmid.cu,mmvq.cu,ggml-cuda.cu,mmq-config-*.cuh}`; `/tmp/ktransformers` (master) — `kt-kernel/operators/amx/{moe_base.hpp,moe.hpp}`, `kt-kernel/cpu_backend/`, `archive/ktransformers/operators/experts.py`, `doc/en/AMX.md`.

## llama.cpp mul_mat_id / MMQ MoE prefill

1. **GPU-side expert compaction, zero host sync** (`mmid.cu`). One CUDA block per expert, one warp scans the ids tensor (templated on n_expert_used ∈ {2,4,6,8,16,32}, warp prefix-scan, packed 22/10-bit smem records) and emits three arrays: `ids_src1` (compact row → source token), `ids_dst` (compact row → final dst row = token*k+slot), `expert_bounds[e:e+1]` (CSR-like bounds). No ids copy to host, no `cudaStreamSynchronize` — the whole MoE prefill is CUDA-graph capturable. The host-sync sort path exists only as the non-MMQ fallback in `ggml-cuda.cu:1868+`.
   *memra portability:* structurally equivalent to memra's expert-major CSR; the item that matters is that llama builds it entirely on-device inside the graph. If memra's CSR grouping involves any host round-trip per layer, this kernel is a direct copy target (~170 lines).

2. **Dedup activation quantization with fused scatter** (PR #25441, merged 2026-07-16; `mmq.cu` `dedup_bcast`). Since gate/up activations are broadcast across the k routed experts, each token is quantized to the MMQ activation format **once** and scattered into all its per-expert compact slots via the inverse map (`quantize_scatter_mmq_q8_1_cuda` / `_fp4_cuda`). Saves k× activation-quantize bandwidth; this is their most recent MoE-prefill win.
   *memra portability:* directly applicable — if memra quantizes/copies the token activation per (token, expert) pair when building CSR-group inputs, switch to quantize-once + scatter. Cheap, exactness-preserving (bit-identical per token).

3. **Variable token-tile width J = 8..128 in steps of 8, picked per launch** (`mmq.cuh` `mul_mat_q_switch_J`, config tables). The weight-row tile is fixed I=128, but the token dimension J is a template parameter chosen at dispatch to minimize the number of column tiles for the actual token count. Ampere/Hopper configs: 256 threads, occupancy 1, ITER_K=256 int8; Blackwell FP4 configs: ITER_K=512. Per expert, tiles with `jt*J >= col_diff` exit immediately.
   *memra portability:* **this is the key structural difference at 65–145 tokens/expert.** memra's fixed 128×128 tile pads a 65-token expert to 128 (≈2× wasted MMA work and activation smem traffic); llama would run J=72 or J=80 there. A small set of J instantiations (e.g. 32/64/80/96/128) over memra's existing 128-row MMQ kernel captures most of it. The same idea shipped for OpenCL as "ragged-tile MoE prefill (skip padded expert tiles)" (PR #25433).

4. **Stream-k decomposition across the full (expert × row-tile × token-tile × k-block) space + fixup kernel** (`mmq.cuh:944+`, per arXiv 2301.03598). Grid = #SMs; each block walks a contiguous range of k-block indices in the flattened space, so uneven tokens-per-expert and partial tiles load-balance automatically; partial-tile results go to a `tmp_fixup` buffer reduced by a second kernel. Reverts to plain tiling when tile-count/SM efficiency ≥ 90% (skips fixup). All Ampere+ configs have stream_k=true.
   *memra portability:* high value. With per-expert CSR groups on H100 (132 SMs), a 128-expert layer at ~1 tile/expert gives ragged waves; stream-k flattens the tail. It composes with (3): fewer padded tiles *and* balanced tiles. Fixup adds a second kernel + buffer — measure per the benchmarks.md discipline; exactness gate matters because split-k changes accumulation order (llama accumulates fixup in f32, same as tile sums, so argmax should hold — still gate it).

5. **Scattered writeback fused into the GEMM epilogue** (`mmq.cuh`: `ids_dst_shared`). Each block loads its J dst-row indices into shared memory and the epilogue writes `dst[ids_dst[j]*stride + i]` directly — no separate gather/scatter kernels around the GEMM, output lands in router order.
   *memra portability:* trivial to adopt if memra currently writes compact per-group output then scatters; deletes a kernel + a round trip of dst traffic.

6. **Native FP4×FP4 MMA path on Blackwell for MXFP4/NVFP4 weights** (`mmq-config-blackwell.cuh`, `quantize_mmq_fp4_cuda`, `block_fp4_mmq`, per-token `y_scale` applied in epilogue; buffer tightened in PR #25613). Activations are quantized to FP4 blocks instead of Q8_1 and the kernel uses Blackwell FP4 tensor cores, K-step 512.
   *memra portability:* 5090 (sm_120a) lane only — this is llama already using the FP4 bw-edge memra's memory notes call out ("copy their kernel structure to match, add FP4/FP8 bw-edge to exceed"). H100 has no FP4 MMA; there llama runs the same int8-MMA MMQ as memra (so the H100 board-loss gap is coming from items 2–5 + Amdahl, not from a magic core). Numeric caution: FP4 activation quantization is a numeric-class change → full argmax + spec self-consistency gates, and it's per-type opt-in in llama (only MXFP4/NVFP4 weights).

7. **MMQ is unconditional for quantized MoE on NVIDIA Turing+** (`ggml_cuda_should_use_mmq`: `if (turing_mma_available(cc)) return true;`). llama never dequant-to-f16 + cuBLAS for quantized experts on modern NVIDIA; the grouped-cublas style path is only the generic fallback (with host syncs). Their reasoning visible in AMD branches: high expert counts make the BLAS path synchronization-bound.
   *memra portability:* evidence point for memra's experimental "dequant active experts to f16 + cublasGemmGroupedBatchedEx" lane — llama.cpp deliberately abandoned that shape on NVIDIA. Worth benchmarking the lane against an MMQ path upgraded with (2)–(5) before investing further; per-layer dequant also costs the write+read of f16 experts that MMQ never pays.

8. **MoE decode**: for n_tokens ≤ per-type limit (mostly 8; NVFP4=8, MXFP4/Q2_K=7, Q3_K=5 on Turing+; `get_mmvq_mmid_max_batch`) it uses **MMVQ with ids**: grid.y = (token × expert-slot) pairs, each block resolves `channel_x = ids[channel_dst]` and runs a dp4a matvec over a few rows; above that it falls into MMQ. Plus graph-level **fused gate+up+GLU matvec** (`ggml_cuda_should_fuse_mul_mat`, valid for SWIGLU/GEGLU/SWIGLU_OAI incl. mul_mat_id + ADD_ID bias): one kernel reads the activation once, produces both projections and applies the glu.
   *memra portability:* memra's warp-per-row dp4a decode is the same family; the gate+up+GLU fusion (one activation read, no intermediate tensors) is the transferable piece if memra still launches gate and up separately at decode/MTP batch sizes. For MTP K=1..8, note llama's per-type crossover table — their measured MMVQ-vs-MMQ break-evens per qtype are free calibration data.

## KTransformers (kt-kernel)

9. **Whole-bank CPU expert offload with AMX INT8/BF16/INT4 GEMM kernels** (`operators/amx/*`): attention/KV/dense on GPU, all expert FFNs in host DRAM. Claimed: 21 TFLOPS BF16 / 35 TOPS INT8 per Xeon-4 socket (~4× PyTorch's AMX path), DeepSeek-V3 prefill 91 → 286+ tok/s, up to 347 tok/s Qwen3-235B prefill, 418 tok/s e2e on Xeon4 + 4090. ## vLLM MoE serving mechanisms — port candidates for memra (prefill-first)

### A. The expert-GEMM prefill core (where memra loses)

**1. moe_align_block_size — token sort + per-BLOCK_M expert mapping (THE central mechanism)**
- How: One cheap CUDA kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/moe_align_sum_kernels.cu`, wrapper `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/moe_align_block_size.py`) takes flattened `topk_ids` (M×topk token-expert pairs), counts tokens per expert in shared memory, CUB BlockScan-prefix-sums the counts *rounded up to BLOCK_SIZE_M*, and scatters into `sorted_token_ids` (token indices grouped by expert, each expert segment padded to a BLOCK_M multiple with sentinel `numel` entries) plus `expert_ids` (one expert index per M-block, -1 for dead blocks) and `num_tokens_post_padded`. Max padding waste is `E*(BLOCK_M-1)` rows, and both GEMM stages (w13 and w2) reuse the same sort. The GEMM then launches ONE grid over all experts: each block reads `expert_ids[pid_m]` to pick its B matrix and gathers A rows via `sorted_token_ids` (`offs_token // top_k` indexes the un-duplicated activation row — activations are never physically replicated for topk).
- Portability: Direct replacement for memra's per-CSR-group dispatch loop on the prefill path. Kills per-expert/per-group launch and tail-quantization overhead: 96 experts × small groups becomes one kernel with block-level indirection (one extra int load per 128×128 tile + gathered A rows). memra's MMQ kernel already has the 128×128 tile machinery; it needs (a) the align/sort kernel (~200 LOC CUDA), (b) A-row gather by `sorted_token_ids` instead of contiguous rows, (c) `expert_ids[pid_m]`-based B base pointer. `expert_ids = -1 → write zeros/skip` maps directly onto the Hy3 REAP pruned-id mask.

**2. Single fused kernel per matmul stage, C shaped [M, topk, N], routed weight in the epilogue**
- How: `fused_moe.py::fused_experts_impl` runs exactly 5 device ops per MoE layer regardless of E: align → GEMM1 (w13, all experts) → silu_mul → GEMM2 (w2, all experts, `MUL_ROUTED_WEIGHT` multiplies the router weight in the epilogue before the store) → `moe_sum` (reduce over topk). Intermediate caches 1 and 3 alias the same allocation. Gate and up projections are one stacked weight `w1: [E, 2N, K]` so GEMM1 produces both halves in one pass.
- Portability: memra's experimental grouped-GEMM lane should adopt the same 5-op skeleton; the router-weight-in-epilogue + topk-major C layout removes a separate scatter-reduce pass. Gate+up merge memra likely has; if not, it's free bandwidth.

**3. GROUP_SIZE_M L2 swizzle + per-M-bucket config autotuning**
- How: Block index is swizzled so GROUP_SIZE_M consecutive M-blocks (same or adjacent experts → same B tiles) are scheduled adjacently for L2 reuse of expert weights. Tile configs come from 327 pre-tuned JSONs (`fused_moe/configs/E=…,N=…,device_name=…,dtype=….json`) keyed by (E, N, device, dtype, block_shape), each mapping an M-grid of batch sizes to {BLOCK_M/N/K, GROUP_SIZE_M, num_warps, num_stages}; lookup picks the nearest M bucket. Defaults when untuned: M≤32→BLOCK_M 16, M≤512→64, else 128; GROUP_SIZE_M 16 only when tokens/expert > 128 (`get_default_config`).
- Portability: memra already runs a tuning campaign; the portable idea is the *M-bucketed config table selected at dispatch time* (chunked prefill means M varies per step: 512-token chunk × topk / E experts ≈ 20-40 tokens/expert on Qwen3.6 — a very different tile than the dense-GEMM assumption). A per-(model, M-bucket) table in the rig config, not a fixed 128×128 tile, is likely worth several tens of percent on the loss cells.

**4. Small-M degradations (decode/MoE interplay, but also small prefill chunks)**
- How: three tiers. (a) `naive_block_assignment` — when `M*topk*4 <= E`, skip the sort entirely; each block is one token (`fused_moe.py::_prepare_expert_assignment`). (b) When `M < BLOCK_M`, cap the launched grid at `M*topk*BLOCK_M` rows so empty expert blocks never launch. (c) `SWAP_AB` on Hopper when BLOCK_M<64: compute Bᵀ·Aᵀ so the token dimension sits in wgmma's flexible N slot instead of the M≥64 slot, then transpose the accumulator (`utils.py::enable_swap_ab`, used in `fused_moe_kernel`). CUTLASS grouped GEMM does the same trick for M≤64 (`grouped_mm_c3x_sm90.cu`, "swap_ab for M <= 64 reduces padding").
- Portability: (a)/(b) are trivial scheduler-level wins for memra's small-batch/spec-decode prefill steps. (c) is the known Hopper wgmma shape problem memra's sm_90a lane already fights; the swap-AB formulation is the concrete fix vLLM ships.

### B. Quantized-expert GEMMs (dequant fused into the mainloop)

**5. Marlin-MoE (`csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/marlin_moe_wna16/marlin_template.h` + `dequant.h`) — the W4A16-class MoE kernel**
- How: Same `sorted_token_ids/expert_ids` interface as the Triton kernel (the sort is computed once in Python, `experts/marlin_moe.py`). Weights stay 4-bit through shared memory; dequant happens **in registers between the smem load and mma.sync**: `lop3`-based bit tricks convert 8 packed int4 → 4 half2 in ~6 ALU ops (FasterTransformer-style magic-bias trick: mask nibbles onto exponent 0x6400, then `__hsub2`/`__hfma2` fuses the zero-point subtraction AND the group scale into the same flop — see the algebra comment at the top of `dequant.h`). Also FP4/FP8 variants where `scale_factor*multiplier` is folded at load time (kNvfp4 is a supported marlin quant type). Work is striped streaming-K style across SMs (`slice_iters/slice_col` machinery) with atomic-add + lock reduction for K-split partials; per-block sorted ids and topk weights are cp.async'd into smem (`read_moe_block_data`); BLOCK_M is chosen by a fill-factor heuristic — smallest of [8,16,32,48,64] with ≥0.9 occupancy of `M*topk/E` (`marlin_moe.py` line ~330).
- Portability: This is the direct answer to "how does dequant integrate with the GEMM rather than a separate pass" — and the direct competitor to memra's experimental dequant-to-f16-then-cublas lane, which writes dequantized experts to HBM and reads them back. A marlin-style register-dequant mainloop eliminates that round trip entirely. For GGUF Q4_0/Q4_K the same lop3+magic-bias sequence applies (llama.cpp-adjacent bit layouts); memra's MMQ int8 path quantizes activations instead — marlin keeps activations fp16/bf16, which matters for memra's exactness gates. Note marlin requires an offline weight repack (tile-interleaved so one 128-bit smem load feeds one thread's mma fragments) — analogous to a one-time GGUF→marlin-layout repack at load.

**6. Machete (`csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/machete/machete_mainloop.cuh`) — Hopper W4A16, NOT used for MoE**
- How: CUTLASS sm90 mixed-input warp-specialized wgmma. Two key ideas: (a) weights are **prepacked** so the values one thread needs across multiple wgmma iterations coalesce into single 128-bit smem loads ("very similar to Marlin's layout, but specific to wgmma"); (b) since wgmma only sources the A operand from registers, they compute Yᵀ = Wᵀ·Xᵀ so the *weights* become A and can be dequantized in registers before feeding tensor cores, while activations ride the TMA/smem B path.
- Portability: vLLM does not route MoE through machete (dense linear layers only) — so for MoE, marlin is the one that ships. But both machete tricks (weights-as-A transpose to enable register dequant under wgmma, prepack-for-128-bit-loads) are exactly the form-sensitive wgmma territory of memra's sm_90a lane; hand-portable, measure every variant per the H100 lane laws.

**7. moe_wna16 CUDA kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/moe_wna16.cu`) — decode-regime 4-bit fallback**
- How: When `tokens*topk/E <= 6` (decode-like), a non-tensor-core kernel: BLOCK_M×BLOCK_K activations staged in smem in a *dequant-order-matched* layout ([0,4,1,5,2,6,3,7] nibble order) so dequantized weight fragments multiply smem activations without shuffles; each thread owns one N column, fp32 accumulation, grid over (m-blocks, n-blocks, k-splits).
- Portability: Same niche as memra's warp-per-row dp4a decode matvecs — memra is already competitive here; low priority. The dequant-order-matched activation staging trick is worth stealing if memra ever adds a W4A16 decode path.

### C. FP8 MoE path (the gemma-26B-A4B 44k tok/s prefill question)

**8. What makes FP8-dynamic MoE prefill fast on 1×H100 — the stack, not one kernel**
- How: The fp8 oracle (`fused_moe/oracle/fp8.py`) picks per-scheme: on Hopper capability-90, single-GPU (no EP), block-quantized FP8 → **the Triton fused_moe_kernel itself** ("On Hopper for Block Fp8, prefer Triton for TP"); per-channel FP8 goes to CUTLASS grouped or DeepGEMM when available. The speed comes from stacking: (a) FP8 tensor cores ≈ 2× BF16 mma throughput and half the weight bytes, using `tl.dot(a, b, acc=accumulator)` for fp8_fast_accum; (b) activations dynamically quantized to FP8 per token-group-128 in a tiny fused kernel (and on the DeepGEMM path, silu_mul + requant to FP8 fused into ONE kernel between the GEMMs — `silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor` in `fp8_utils.py`); (c) blockwise 128×128 weight scales applied per-K-iteration inside the mainloop (two extra loads + one FMA per tile); (d) everything else is mechanism #1/#2/#3 — one launch, sorted tokens, tuned tiles. The CUTLASS alternative (`experts/cutlass_moe.py` + `grouped_mm_c3x_sm90.cu`) physically permutes tokens to expert-contiguous order (`moe_permute`), computes per-expert problem sizes **on device** from `expert_first_token_offset` (no host sync, CUDA-graph safe), and runs a ptr-array pingpong warp-specialized FP8FastAccum grouped GEMM with per-M-range tile specializations (M≤4, M≤64, default 64×256×128).
- Portability: memra's H100 lane is losing the gemma cell against exactly this. Two routes: (i) match the structure — int8 MMQ is already ~FP8-class MACs, so the gap is likely the *pipeline* (per-group launches, separate dequant/act/quant passes, unfused router weight), i.e. port mechanisms 1-3 + fused act-requant; (ii) for the H100 lane specifically, an FP8-weights path with dynamic per-token-group activation quant would match vLLM's arithmetic rate — but that's a numeric-class change gated by argmax/spec-consistency. The on-device problem-size computation from expert offsets is directly portable to memra's cublasGemmGroupedBatchedEx lane today (removes host round-trip for group sizes; permute-to-contiguous beats gather-per-group for A operand TMA/coalescing).

**9. DeepGEMM m-grouped contiguous layout (Hopper FP8 alternative)**
- How: `experts/deep_gemm_moe.py`: instead of block-indirection inside the kernel, tokens are permuted into an expert-contiguous buffer where each expert's row count is rounded up to the GEMM's BLOCK_M (128) alignment (`compute_aligned_M`), then a JIT'd `m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_contiguous` runs with a per-128-row expert index. Chooses per-call the smaller BLOCK_M when expected tokens/expert is small.
- Portability: Same padding idea as mechanism 1, but with physically contiguous A — better TMA behavior at the cost of a permute copy. Worth an A/B against the gather variant on memra's H100 lane; padding waste at 96 experts × 128 alignment is significant for small chunks, which is why they gate on `align <= M`.

### D. Chunked prefill + layout interplay

**10. Chunked prefill bounds M; MoE config and workspaces key off the chunk**
- How: vLLM's scheduler caps each step at `max_num_batched_tokens`, so the MoE layer sees M ≤ chunk size; the tuned-config lookup (mechanism 3) and workspace allocation (`modular_kernel.py::_allocate_buffers`, workspace13/workspace2 reused across layers via a workspace manager) are sized to that M. The align/sort runs per layer per step (routing differs per layer) — it's cheap enough (~O(M·topk)) that this is fine. No cross-chunk expert-weight persistence is attempted for fits-in-VRAM models; the win is purely that every chunk executes the fully-fused path with tiles tuned for that M regime.
- Portability: For memra: pick prefill chunk size jointly with the MoE tile config so tokens/expert lands in a tuned bucket (e.g. chunk 2048 × topk8 / 96E = ~170 tokens/expert → full 128-wide tiles), and keep per-layer sort on-GPU with no host sync so it fuses into the graph.

**11. Expert weight layout choices**
- How: All non-marlin paths store experts stacked `[E, N, K]` row-major, K contiguous (`stride(-1)==1` asserted), gate+up merged into `w1=[E, 2N, K]`, w2=[E, K, N]; expert selection is just `base + expert_id * stride_be`. Scales stacked `[E, ...]` identically. Marlin/machete add an offline tile-interleaved repack per expert. Activations are never expanded topk-fold — the `// top_k` gather trick (mechanism 1) reads each token row once per assigned expert straight from the original hidden_states.
- Portability: memra's GGUF expert-major layout is already compatible with the `stride_be` model; the actionable deltas are (a) merged gate_up stacking and (b) ensuring the SLRU-cache/resident-slab layouts keep experts at fixed strides so one kernel launch can index all resident experts without a pointer table when the bank is uniform.

- One GPU kernel sorts the flattened `topk_ids` by expert and pads each expert's token run to `BLOCK_SIZE_M`, producing `sorted_token_ids` (padded index list), `expert_ids` (one expert id **per M-block**), `num_tokens_post_padded`. Cost: one small CUDA kernel, no CPU sync.

**A3. `c_sorted` / TMA down-GEMM: keep the intermediate in expert-sorted order between the two GEMMs.**
File: `moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py` (`down_moe_use_tma`, `c_sorted=True`).

### B. Two-batch overlap (TBO) — and what it means at one GPU

Blog + `docs/advanced_features/expert_parallelism.md`. Mechanism: split each batch into two micro-batches; express the layer as an ops list with explicit yield points (`attn → yield → dispatch → mlp → yield → combine`); interleave so micro-batch A's **compute** hides micro-batch B's **communication**. Critical detail: submit GPU compute work *before* the CPU-blocking dispatch call so the compute stream never drains (launch-order, not stream-priority, is the fix). Gains: 27–35% prefill throughput, plus halved peak activation memory (enabled 16k tokens/device vs 8k OOM).
- At EP=1 there is no NVLink/RDMA leg, but the structure ports to memra's real overlap axes:
  1. **Compute/compute overlap of unlike phases:** attention (bandwidth-lean at prefill? no — but MoE FFN is compute; attention is memory/compute mixed) — pair micro-batch A's attention with micro-batch B's expert GEMM on separate streams so tensor-core (MMQ) and softmax/vector work co-schedule. This is the same reasoning as FA3's inter-warpgroup overlap, applied inter-batch.
  2. **Weight-movement overlap for spill:** the "communication" leg at one GPU is NVMe→host→HBM expert fetch. **C1. Masked grouped GEMM at EP=1 for decode/CUDA-graph.** In `moe_runner/deep_gemm.py`, the **standard (non-EP) dispatch** path packs tokens into a fixed `[E, m_max, K]` tensor (`moe_ep_deepgemm_preprocess` → `masked_m`, `expected_m`, `src2dst`) and runs the **masked** grouped GEMM — shape is static, so the whole MoE layer is CUDA-graph capturable with token counts known only on-GPU. At EP=1 the comm legs become the scatter/gather epilogues — the single-GPU reading is: a persistent fused kernel where the scatter, both GEMMs, and activation are phases of one launch. ### D. DeepGEMM grouped/masked GEMM design (variable tokens-per-expert)

Two layouts, chosen by phase:
- **m-grouped contiguous** (prefill): only the **M axis** is grouped; N and K fixed across experts (all experts same shape). All experts' tokens are concatenated into one `[sum_m, K]` tensor; each expert segment **must be padded to the GEMM block-M alignment** (`get_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout()`). The kernel takes an `m_indices` int32 tensor of length `sum_m` (expert id per row, padding rows = id of the pad target / -1); each m-tile reads its group id and selects the corresponding expert's B. Variable tokens-per-expert is thus handled purely by **data layout + a per-row index tensor**, never by per-group launch or CPU-visible shapes. SGLang's `ep_scatter` builds `input_tensor`, `m_indices`, `output_index` in one Triton kernel; `ep_gather` does the weighted combine.
- **masked layout** (decode / CUDA graph): fixed `[num_groups, m_max, K]` allocation; `masked_m[g]` (GPU tensor) gives the valid row count per group; kernel computes only valid tiles. `expected_m` (CPU int, a hint) selects block config. Pairs with sources that write counts GPU-side. Cost: over-allocation to `m_max`; SGLang caps it (`SGLANG_OPT_DG_MASKED_M_CAP`) under memory pressure.
- Both are JIT-specialized per exact shape (NVRTC/nvcc at runtime, shape-keyed cache) — SM90/SM100 only as shipped (wgmma/UMMA + TMA), so the **kernels don't run on sm_120a; the layout contracts do.**
- Portability for memra: the contiguous contract is nearly isomorphic to memra's expert-major CSR — the two deltas worth adopting are (1) **pad each CSR group to the MMQ tile-M (128) so every tile is expert-pure** and the kernel needs only a per-tile expert id (kills intra-tile divergence and per-group launches in both MMQ and the cublas grouped lane — note `cublasGemmGroupedBatchedEx` already eats per-group m, so padding matters only for the custom kernel), and (2) the **masked variant for graphed decode/MTP** (C1). SGLang's grouped-GEMM+TBO combination is what their blog credits for the 3.3x prefill gain over TP16 — mechanism-wise, for memra the analog claim is: expert-pure tiles + sorted-intermediate (A3) + fused requant (A4) is the prefill package aimed exactly at the two losing H100 cells.

# memra MoE sweep synthesis

**Gain budget (frame every magnitude against this):** the losses are 0.92x (q35) and 0.89x (g26) e2e, both expert-prefill-bound. If prefill is ~50-70% of those cells' e2e time, flipping them needs roughly **15-30% MoE-prefill-throughput gain** — not 2x. Several levers below claim overlapping waste; they do not stack multiplicatively. Every numeric-path lever passes kernel-check + run-gen argmax + run-spec K=1..8, interleaved x5 on-box.

**Already has — do not re-implement:** expert-major CSR grouping (the moe_align/sort *concept*), int8-MMA quantized-weight GEMM (the Marlin/wna16 *niche*), SLRU expert residency (Report 2 confirms KTransformers has nothing better — no prefetch exists in kt-kernel), MTP spec decode, dp4a decode matvecs, prefill/decode kernel split, pinned-host + CUDA-owner-thread H2D spill discipline, on-rig tuning infra, quantized KV + parked-session reuse pool, REAP masked-id contract (identical semantics to vLLM `expert_ids=-1` / SGLang `filter_expert`).

## 1. Ranked prefill levers (gain/cost)

**1. Ragged token-tiles (variable J) + small-M grid capping — R2 #3, R0 #4. Cost: S-M.**
The regime on these cells is ~20-45 tokens/expert (512-chunk × top-k / 96-128E, R0's arithmetic; R2 says 65-145). memra's fixed 128-token tile pads that to 128 → **2-4x wasted MMA work and smem traffic on the exact bound resource**. llama.cpp dispatches J∈{8..128, step 8} per launch; a handful of instantiations (32/64/80/96/128) over the existing MMQ captures most of it. This is the single most direct attack on the loss cells; capturing even half the padding waste plausibly covers the entire 8-11% gap alone. Note llama runs the *same int8-MMA* on H100 (R2 #6/#7) — the board gap is this + items 2-4, not a magic core.

**2. Single-launch block-indirected expert GEMM with fused gather/scatter — R0 #1/#2, R1 A1, R2 #1/#5. Cost: M.**
All three engine reports converge: one kernel per GEMM stage per layer over ALL experts — per-tile `expert_ids[pid_m]` B-pointer, A-row gather via `sorted_token_ids // topk` (no activation replication), router weight in the GEMM-2 epilogue, dst-scatter via smem ids, one moe_sum. Conditional: if memra's CSR pair path already launches once over all groups, this collapses to just the gather/epilogue pieces; if it loops per group (96-128 launches/layer × 2 stages), this is the structural gap vs vLLM's 44k gemma number. Also make the id-compaction fully on-device, zero host sync (llama's `mmid.cu`, ~170 lines) so the whole layer graphs.

**3. Expert-sorted intermediate through the whole layer + fused SwiGLU/requant + quantize-once — R1 A3/A4, R2 #2. Cost: S each.**
Keep gate/up output in expert-sorted padded order, run activation over it skipping pad blocks, feed GEMM-2 with *dense* A-loads; only one scatter per layer. Fuse SwiGLU + int8-requant into one kernel; quantize activations once per layer pre-gather (top-k reads share it — saves (k−1)× quant passes; this dedup was llama's most recent shipped MoE-prefill win, so expect single-digit % but nearly free and bit-identical). SonicMoE (R3) quantifies the family: gather+epilogue fusion = 1.86x kernel vs ScatterMoE — treat that as the ceiling of levers 2+3 combined, not additive.

**4. M-bucketed tile-config table at dispatch + chunk/tile co-tuning — R0 #3/#10, R1 A5. Cost: S (infra exists).**
vLLM ships 327 tuned JSONs keyed on (E,N,device,dtype,M-bucket); the portable idea is picking BLOCK_M/N/K per actual chunk-M, and choosing the prefill chunk so tokens/expert lands in a tuned bucket (e.g. 2048×8/96 ≈ 170 → full tiles). R0's "several tens of percent" claim is unverified — but the sweep is cheap on existing infra and partially subsumes lever 1.

**5. Stream-K across (expert × tile × k) + fixup — R2 #4, corroborated by KT work-stealing #12. Cost: M.**
Flattens ragged waves across 132 SMs at ~1 tile/expert; llama defaults it on for all Ampere+. Expect ~5-15% kernel-level on skewed layers. Changes accumulation order → full exactness gates.

**6. Decide the cublas dequant-f16 lane's fate — R2 #7, R0 #5. Cost: S (the benchmark), negative if killed.**
llama.cpp deliberately abandoned dequant+BLAS for quantized MoE on NVIDIA (sync-bound at high E; pays HBM write+read MMQ never pays). Per flags doctrine: A/B it against MMQ+levers 1-3; if it loses, kill the lane. Marlin-style register-dequant (lop3 magic-bias, NVFP4 supported) is what that lane would have to become to win — cost L, only if the A/B says the f16 path has legs.

**7. Merged gate+up stacked weight [E, 2N, K] — R0 #2/#11, R3 TritonMoE (35% global-traffic cut for the pair). Cost: S-M.** Check whether memra already stacks; if GGUF keeps separate gate/up tensors, this is free bandwidth via a load-time repack.

**8. H100-only: SWAP_AB for BLOCK_M<64 (compute BᵀAᵀ so tokens sit in wgmma's N slot) — R0 #4/#6. Cost: M.** The concrete fix for the known sm_90a small-M wgmma shape problem; form-sensitive, measure every variant per lane law.

**9. 5090-only "exceed" step: FP4 activation quant × NVFP4 weights on FP4 tensor cores — R2 #6. Cost: M-L.** llama already ships this (ITER_K=512, per-token y_scale epilogue). Numeric-class change, full gate battery; per-type opt-in.

**10. KV host tier + chunk-hashed prefix keys — R4 #1/#2. Cost: M.** Explicitly does **not** move the cold pp512 board cells (R4's own caveat) — it moves multi-turn/shared-system-prompt serving. Worth doing, wrong lever for the two losses; rank accordingly.

## 2. Decode levers (>10% potential only)

- **Fused gate+up+GLU matvec** (R2 #8): one activation read produces both projections + GLU, no intermediates — only if memra currently launches gate and up separately at decode; if so, plausibly >10% of MoE-FFN decode time on A3B/A4B models.
- **Masked fixed-shape grouped GEMM for graphed MTP verify** (R1 C1, D): `[E, m_max, K]` with GPU-side `masked_m` makes router-variant MoE CUDA-graph-capturable and turns K=1..8 verify into one small-M grouped GEMM instead of k matvec passes.
